claim: Let \(K\) be a finite nonempty simplicial complex. Let \(\widetilde\gamma(K)\) be its simplicial total-domination number, with value \(+\infty\) if no totally dominating set exists, and let \(\kappa(K)=\sup\{r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge -1}:K\text{ is }r\text{-conic}\}\). Then \(\kappa(K)=\widetilde\gamma(K)-1\), with \(+\infty-1=+\infty\). Moreover, for finite nonempty complexes \(K,L\), \(\widetilde\gamma(K*L)=\widetilde\gamma(K)+\widetilde\gamma(L)\) and hence \(\kappa(K*L)=\kappa(K)+\kappa(L)+1\), with the usual \(+\infty\) conventions.
integrity: The proof gives both logical directions of r-conicity versus total domination and proves join additivity directly. A separate exhaustive verifier checks all 126 labeled complexes on at most four declared vertices and 144 small join pairs; these finite checks are corroboration, not the general proof.
scientific_limitations: The identity is elementary once the definitions are juxtaposed. It does not claim new sharp connectivity bounds beyond consequences of existing conicity theorems, and an unindexed post-2021 equivalent observation remains a residual literature risk.
title: Conicity equals total domination minus one, with exact join additivity
